indicator_definition: This indicator measures the proportion of adults aged 25 to 64 who participated in formal or non-formal education and training in the four weeks preceding the survey. It is expressed as a percentage of the total population aged 25 to 64. Data are based on the EU Labour Force Survey.
rationale: Life-long learning is essential for adapting to a changing labour market and maintaining employability. Higher participation in adult learning reduces skills mismatches and supports social inclusion. The goal is to increase the proportion of adults engaged in continuous learning throughout their lives.
methodology_characteristics: Data are collected through the EU Labour Force Survey (EU-LFS). Formal education refers to education provided by the regular system of schools, universities and other formal educational institutions. Non-formal education includes all organised educational activities outside the formal educational system.
